tasks.short: Collect patterns from cases, meet municipal and community partners about gaps, write policy advice, present it and keep the list of community services current.

steps.what: Hospital social worker tallies case patterns such as discharge delays in a spreadsheet
Hospital social worker meets municipal and community partners to assist in community development
Hospital social worker writes advice on social policy
Hospital social worker presents the advice to the board or municipality
Hospital social worker keeps a list of community services and contacts

tasks.design: A dashboard on the case system ({BI}) shows anonymised counts of reasons for delayed discharge and unmet needs per month, so patterns no longer need tallying. The municipality's shared social map ({OTHER}) replaces the private contact list. Meeting partners, writing advice and presenting it stay with the social worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patterns were tallied by hand and contact lists kept per worker.
tasks.enabler_now: Case systems feed dashboards, and municipalities keep shared social maps.
tasks.still_hard: Policy change depends on relationships and timing, not data alone.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which alderman will listen to a story more than a chart.

reach.learn: Whether shared delay figures speed up community fixes.

evidence.claim: Case systems can feed dashboards with anonymised counts per month.
Health data are special category data; policy work uses anonymised counts only.

assumptions: Boundary: from case patterns to presented advice; the policy decision is outside.
Input contract: delay reasons recorded in the case system by social workers; social map kept by the municipality; fallback is spreadsheets.
Meetings, writing and presenting do not change.
Partners' time is outside the social worker's savings.
research_questions: Do partners act on the delay figures?

already_counted.description: Hospital social worker reads the dashboard.

incremental.description: Hospital social worker records delay reasons consistently.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is meetings and writing advice.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search the literature, design the study and get ethics approval, interview patients and colleagues, collect questionnaires, transcribe and code interviews and write up the findings.

steps.what: Hospital social worker searches the literature on the research question

loop.input: The research question and abstracts from the library's licensed databases.
loop.output: A short list of relevant studies with a one-line reason each.
loop.check: Code keeps only studies found in the library databases with a working link; the social worker reads each abstract.
loop.stop: One list per search; the social worker searches by hand when the list is empty.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search misses studies that use other terms for the same issue.

steps.what: Hospital social worker designs the study and applies for ethics review
Hospital social worker interviews patients and colleagues
Hospital social worker types in paper questionnaire answers
Hospital social worker transcribes and codes the interviews

loop.input: Interview audio recorded with the participant's consent.
loop.output: A verbatim transcript with speaker turns and unclear words marked.
loop.check: The social worker checks each transcript against the audio before coding; recordings are deleted after checking.
loop.stop: One pass per recording; poor audio is transcribed by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Speech cannot be turned into text with fixed rules.

steps.what: Hospital social worker writes up research findings to advance knowledge in the field

tasks.design: A literature desk over the library's licensed databases returns studies with a reason each, and the social worker reads every abstract. Questionnaires run online ({OTHER}) so answers arrive as data. Interviews are transcribed by speech recognition inside the hospital's environment and checked against the audio. Designing, interviewing, coding and writing stay with the social worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Searching, typing questionnaires and transcribing took most of the research hours.
tasks.enabler_now: Literature tools, online questionnaires and speech recognition are available to hospitals.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who are ill or have low literacy need paper or interviews.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a family does not say about caring at home.
tasks.altitude: The social worker reads shortlists and checks transcripts instead of producing them.

reach.learn: Whether transcription frees time for analysis.

evidence.claim: Speech recognition and literature search tools can produce transcripts and study shortlists.
Health data are special category data; research use needs a legal basis and safeguards.
Research with patients may need review by a medical ethics committee.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the report; publication is outside.
Input contract: abstracts from the hospital library's databases; consent from participants; fallback is hand search and typing.
Designing, interviewing and writing do not change.
Recordings stay inside the hospital's environment.
research_questions: How long does transcript checking take per hour of audio?

already_counted.description: Hospital social worker reads each listed abstract.
Hospital social worker checks transcripts against the audio.

incremental.description: Hospital social worker sets up the online questionnaire.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Studies with paper questionnaires save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather signals of child abuse from staff, talk with the child and parents, consult the national advice centre, decide on protective action, document every step and make the report.

steps.what: Hospital social worker gathers signals from doctors and nurses
Hospital social worker investigates child abuse or neglect by talking with the child and parents
Hospital social worker consults the advice centre and colleagues by phone
Hospital social worker decides on reporting or protective action
Hospital social worker documents signals, talks and decisions in the case file
Hospital social worker writes the report for the advice centre
Hospital social worker sends the report to the advice centre

tasks.design: A structured form in the patient record system ({OTHER}) follows the steps of the reporting code, with fields for signals, conversations, consultations and decisions and restricted access. The report to the advice centre is built from that form and sent through the secure channel, which the social worker completes and sends. Investigating, consulting and deciding stay with the social worker; no AI scores risk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were kept in free text in several places and the report written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems hold structured forms with restricted access.
tasks.still_hard: Every case differs; the form must not push towards a box-ticking judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Talking with a frightened parent so the child stays safe and the family stays in care.

reach.learn: Whether a shared form improves signal recording.

evidence.claim: Record systems hold structured forms with access limited to named roles.
Professionals follow the steps of the reporting code for domestic violence and child abuse before reporting.
Decisions with significant effect may not rest solely on automated processing.

assumptions: Boundary: from staff concerns to the report made; actions by the advice centre are outside.
Input contract: form fields set by the hospital's child protection lead; fallback is free-text notes.
Investigating, consulting and deciding do not change.
No AI reads or scores these cases.
research_questions: Are case files complete when reviewed?

incremental.description: Hospital social worker learns the structured form.

approvals.approved_version: The report as written and checked by the social worker in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is conversation and judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Work out which care scheme applies after discharge, fill in the application, gather and check attachments, submit it, track the decision and file it in the record.

steps.what: Hospital social worker works out which care scheme covers care after discharge
Hospital social worker fills in the application paperwork for long-term care or home support

loop.input: Demographics, diagnoses and the nursing and medical notes of the current admission.
loop.output: A prefilled form with a draft care-needs section, each statement linked to a dated note.
loop.check: Code flags any statement without a linked note and any risk statement absent from the notes; the social worker edits and approves every section.
loop.stop: One draft per application; nothing is submitted without approval.
loop.why_not_simpler: Care needs are written across free-text notes that rules cannot summarise.

steps.what: Hospital social worker gathers medical statements and checks the complete application
Hospital social worker uploads the application to the assessing body's portal
Hospital social worker tracks application status and chases decisions
Hospital social worker files the decision in the patient record

tasks.design: A decision table in the case system ({OTHER}) suggests the care scheme from the discharge plan for the social worker to confirm. A bounded step prefills the application and drafts the care-needs section from the admission's notes, linking each statement to a note; the social worker edits every section. Attachments from the record are added automatically, and once the social worker has checked the complete application, it is uploaded to the assessing body's portal ({GOV_PORTAL}). A status list with deadline alerts replaces chasing from memory, and decisions are filed automatically. The assessing body decides eligibility.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applications were written from scratch and status tracked by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can draft summaries from notes, and case systems link attachments and deadlines.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted care needs can miss what matters; reports have contained invented statements.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to a family why a nursing home is the safe choice.
tasks.altitude: The social worker edits a prefilled application instead of writing it.

reach.learn: Whether faster applications shorten delayed discharges.

evidence.claim: In a Somerset Council pilot with 20 staff, practitioners self-reported about 11 hours a week saved and weekly admin time down 46%.
Social workers found invented content in AI-generated notes.
Eligibility decisions may not rest solely on automated processing.

assumptions: Boundary: from the discharge plan to the decision on file; the eligibility decision is outside.
Input contract: discharge plan from the ward; notes in the patient record; decision table kept by the social work team lead; fallback is writing by hand.
The social worker approves every section before submission.
Assessing bodies' time is outside the social worker's savings.
research_questions: How much of the drafted care-needs text does the social worker keep?

already_counted.description: Hospital social worker confirms the suggested scheme.
Hospital social worker edits the drafted care-needs section.
Hospital social worker checks the complete application.

incremental.description: Hospital social worker keeps the decision table current.

approvals.approved_version: The complete application as checked by the social worker in s3; changes need a new check before upload.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The hospital social worker keeps conversations, protection decisions and advice; tallies, typing and application paperwork shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A social worker who spends saved hours with patients and families before discharge.
